_README: Bio clause templates (CCB-S4-006). VERSIONED DATA; the loader refuses a set without
a version. This is the FOURTH authored set after the archetypes, the style loadings
and the coverage regions, and the previous three all acquired structure nobody
intended. Assume this one has too until verify:bio says otherwise.
CLAUSES, NOT WHOLE-BIO SKELETONS. A fixed set of skeletons with substituted words is
the obvious implementation and the obvious failure: it passes line by line and
collapses in aggregate, which is what a reader scrolling a member list actually
notices. A bio here composes 1 to 3 clauses from a pool and then varies the
separator, the capitalisation, the terminal punctuation and the emoji. Composition is
only the first of those mechanisms, which is what section 6 asks for.
FRAGMENTS ARE FIRST-CLASS. Real bios are frequently not sentences at all, so each
theme carries both fragment clauses and sentence clauses and the generator chooses
between them rather than always producing prose.
LANGUAGE FOLLOWS originBlend, NOT A GLOBAL SETTING (section 7). English and German
are authored. An origin mapping to a language with no pool falls back, and the
fallback rate is COUNTED and reported rather than hidden, because a population with a
German-Spanish origin mix having uniformly English bios is exactly the failure the
requirement names.
NO SIMULATED NON-NATIVE SPEECH. The specification withdrew that register because it
drifts into caricature and has no empirical support. Every avatar writes its language
plainly and sentenceComplexity carries whatever variation is needed.
EMOJI HERE ARE NOT THE EIGHT VERIFIED REACTION EMOJI. Those constrain what the core
accepts as a reaction, not what a profile description may contain (section 8).
INTERESTS ARE TRANSLATED PER LANGUAGE. An English interest inside a German sentence is
the same failure section 7 names one layer down, and the numeric checks passed while
the text said 'arbeite an cooking'. Reading the output is what caught it.
CLAUSES CARRY NO TERMINAL PUNCTUATION OF THEIR OWN. It is stripped before joining and
reapplied once at the end, because terminal punctuation is one of the six variety
mechanisms and a clause supplying its own produced 'in 2019.. i am legally required'.
